options.opd: High-resolution CT scan of the chest

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Chronic productive cough" -> "Yellow-green sputum" -> "Possible bronchiectasis" -> "High-resolution CT scan of the chest" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Chronic cough with sputum" -> "History of dyspnea" -> "Possible mycobacterial infection" -> "Mycobacterial sputum culture" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Chronic cough" -> "Digital clubbing" -> "Possible cystic fibrosis" -> "Sweat chloride test" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Chronic cough" -> "Expiratory wheezes" -> "Possible obstructive lung disease" -> "Pulmonary function tests" -> 55%
analysis: The patient's symptoms and history suggest a chronic lung condition characterized by productive cough, dyspnea, and digital clubbing. The presence of large amounts of yellow-green sputum and occasional blood streaks, along with the history of improvement with antibiotics, points towards a condition like bronchiectasis. High-resolution CT scan of the chest is the most appropriate test to confirm the diagnosis of bronchiectasis, as it can reveal the characteristic bronchial dilation and other structural changes in the lungs.
